Subject: Dedicated capacity intake - initial traffic & concurrency checklist

Hi Amit —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. To give you the fastest, defensible sizing for a Dedicated pool we usually start with a short intake. I attached a tiny CSV (capacity-intake-template.csv) but below are the specific items that change sizing dramatically — if you can reply with ballpark numbers it will let us convert to GPU counts and a preliminary cost range within 48 hours.

Quick asks (short answers ok):
- Typical sustained QPS (requests/sec) during business hours
- Observed peak QPS (burst) and how long bursts last (minutes)
- Concurrent active sessions you expect (simultaneous requests that need KV/cache per user)
- Percent of requests that are streaming vs final-chunk only (e.g., 40% streaming)
- Avg prompt length (tokens) and avg response length (tokens)
- Max context length we need to support (tokens)
- Are requests batchable on the client side? (yes/no)
- Data residency / SOC2 / PII notes if relevant
- Target latency SLO (p50/p95) or max acceptable tail latency

Example assumptions I’ll use unless you tell me otherwise: models in the 13B–70B family, 2–4s p50 for generative flows, use of KV caching for long sessions, and occasional 1–2 minute burst windows up to 10x sustained. If you can paste a short sample of an hour of traffic (CSV) that’s great — otherwise the bullets above work.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Dev and Maya for a rapid sizing once we have your numbers.

—Jordan

Jordan —

Thanks — answers below (quick, high level; I attached a CSV with one hour of anonymized request logs). Happy to clarify on a call.

- Sustained QPS: ~40 req/s (weekday 09:00–18:00)
- Peak QPS (bursts): ~360 req/s for ~5–15 minutes during marketing pushes (we see 9x bursts)
- Concurrent active sessions: ~80 concurrent sessions at peak (many are chat sessions with KV)
- Streaming: ~65% streaming (token-at-a-time delivery for customer chat UX)
- Avg prompt length: 180 tokens (user + system + metadata)
- Avg response length: 420 tokens
- Max context length required: 8192 tokens for some long-ticket histories (not all requests)
- Batchable: minimal ability to batch on client side (most are low-latency chat messages)
- Security: SOC2 compliance required; customer data is sensitive but we can pseudonymize; data residency must be US-only for now
- Latency SLO: target p95 < 2.5s for non-streaming; p95 stream-first-chunk < 400ms

Attached: sample-traffic.csv (hour of traffic, anonymized).

Let me know if you need histograms or a longer sample.

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity intake - preliminary sizing peek

Jordan / team / Amit —

Thanks for the data, Amit — useful sample. I ran quick back-of-envelope sizing with two target model scenarios and a few conservative assumptions. This is a preliminary, non-binding estimate meant to get us into the right ballpark for Dedicated procurement.

Assumptions used (conservative):
- Model choices: quantized 13B (FP16->int8 path) and 70B (FP16) as two reference points
- Streaming overhead: additional 20% CPU/network overhead vs non-streaming requests
- KV cache: active session cache assumed for 80 concurrent sessions; cache hit rate 65%
- Token processing throughput: measured effective token/s per GPU (approx) — 13B quantized: ~6k tokens/sec; 70B FP16: ~1.2k tokens/sec
- Average tokens per request = prompt(180) + response(420) = 600 tokens

Calculations (peak 360 qps):
- Tokens/sec at peak = 360 * 600 = 216,000 tokens/sec
- GPUs required (13B quantized) = 216,000 / 6,000 ≈ 36 GPUs (allowing 20% headroom -> 44 GPUs)
- GPUs required (70B FP16) = 216,000 / 1,200 ≈ 180 GPUs (with 20% headroom -> 216 GPUs)

Recommendation:
- If CleverRetail can accept a quantized 13B family model with Redwood-verified quality checks, start with a 44-GPU A100/H100 pool sized for 13B quantized. This meets the p95 latency target for non-streaming and gives good cost economics.
- If strict fidelity requires 70B-class models, we should propose a staged rollout: reserve a smaller H100-backed 70B fallback pool (e.g., 24 GPUs) for critical queries and route lower-fidelity traffic to the 13B pool. This hybrid approach reduces committed spend and gives a path to full fidelity when needed.

Risks / notes:
- 8192 token contexts push memory; 70Bs at full context may require multi-GPU sharding (increases complexity).
- Streaming increases CPU and connection concurrency — ensure load balancers and websocket infrastructure are sized for sustained connection counts (~80+ concurrent sessions).
- If bursts are frequent and cost is a concern, implement rate-limited burst windows + autoscale in Dedicated with short warm-up (we can demo burst handling).

Next steps:
1) Quick call (30 minutes) to confirm model fidelity tradeoffs and acceptable ops complexity.
2) If they accept 13B quantized baseline, I can produce a formal Dedicated sizing deck and a cost estimate for a 12-month reserved pool.
3) If 70B fidelity is mandatory, we'll scope a hybrid proof-of-concept to validate latency at scale.

Attaching a short PDF with the same numbers and rough cost ranges.
